source_refs.note: Exercise 4.2, Question 5: Find values of x, parts (i)-(iii) (book page 60).

blocks.prompt: 5 (i) Find values of \(x\) if: \(\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 & x \\ -1 & -3 & -4 \\ x & 1 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = -30\)
blocks.explanation:
The determinant contains \(x\); expanding it gives a quadratic in \(x\).
Setting it equal to \(-30\) gives an equation to solve.
Plan: expand along row 1, simplify, solve; test the discriminant.
steps:
Given: \(\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 & x \\ -1 & -3 & -4 \\ x & 1 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = -30\)
To find: the values of \(x\).
Method: Expand along row 1 (signs \(+,\,-,\,+\)) to get \(ax^2 + bx + c\); then solve the quadratic equation.

Minors of row 1
\[M_{11} = (-3)(0) - (-4)(1) = 4\]
\[M_{12} = (-1)(0) - (-4)(x) = 4x\]
\[M_{13} = (-1)(1) - (-3)(x) = 3x - 1\]
Why: Cover row 1 and each column in turn; treat \(x\) like a number.

Expand
\[\Delta = 3(4) - 1(4x) + x(3x - 1)\]
\[= 12 - 4x + 3x^2 - x\]
\[= 3x^2 - 5x + 12\]
Why: Entries \(3, 1, x\) with signs \(+,\,-,\,+\); collect like terms.

Form the equation
\[3x^2 - 5x + 12 = -30\]
\[3x^2 - 5x + 42 = 0\]
Why: Add 30 to both sides.

Discriminant
\[b^2 - 4ac = 25 - 4(3)(42)\]
\[= 25 - 504 = -479 < 0\]
Why: With \(a = 3,\ b = -5,\ c = 42\). A negative discriminant means no real root.

Roots (complex)
\[x = \dfrac{5 \pm \sqrt{-479}}{6}\]
\[= \dfrac{5 \pm i\sqrt{479}}{6}\]
Why: Quadratic formula \(x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\); \(\sqrt{-479} = i\sqrt{479}\) (Unit 1).
blocks.final_answer: As printed, there is no real value of \(x\); the roots are \(x = \frac{5 \pm i\sqrt{479}}{6}\).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(x = 2\) or \(-1\). These do not fit the printed question: the determinant equals \(3x^2 - 5x + 12\), which is \(14\) at \(x = 2\) and \(20\) at \(x = -1\), never \(-30\). The printed question (an entry or the right-hand side) must contain a misprint. As printed, \(3x^2 - 5x + 42 = 0\) has no real root; its roots are \(\frac{5 \pm i\sqrt{479}}{6}\).

blocks.prompt: 5 (ii) Find values of \(x\) if: \(\begin{vmatrix} 1 & x-1 & 3 \\ -1 & x+1 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & x \end{vmatrix} = 0\)
blocks.explanation:
Again the determinant contains \(x\) and must equal 0.
Plan: expand along row 1, collect the terms into a quadratic, solve.
steps:
Given: \(\begin{vmatrix} 1 & x-1 & 3 \\ -1 & x+1 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & x \end{vmatrix} = 0\)
To find: the values of \(x\).
Method: Expansion along row 1, then the quadratic formula.

Solve
\[2x^2 - 2x + 5 = 0\]
\[b^2 - 4ac = 4 - 40 = -36 < 0\]
\[x = \dfrac{2 \pm 6i}{4} = \dfrac{1 \pm 3i}{2}\]
Why: Negative discriminant: no real root; the quadratic formula gives complex roots, \(\sqrt{-36} = 6i\).

Check
\[x = 0:\ \Delta = 5,\quad x = 1:\ \Delta = 5\]
Why: These are the key's values; they make \(\Delta = 5\), not 0 (see the correction below).
blocks.final_answer: As printed, there is no real value of \(x\); the roots are \(x = \frac{1 \pm 3i}{2}\).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(x = 0\) or \(1\). These do not fit the printed question: at \(x = 0\) and at \(x = 1\) the determinant equals \(2x^2 - 2x + 5 = 5\), not 0. The key's values would be right if the question read "\(= 5\)". As printed, \(2x^2 - 2x + 5 = 0\) has no real root; its roots are \(\frac{1 \pm 3i}{2}\).

blocks.prompt: 5 (iii) Find values of \(x\) if: \(\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & x & 2 \\ 3 & 6 & x \end{vmatrix} = 0\)
blocks.explanation:
The determinant contains \(x\) twice on the diagonal and must equal 0.
Row 1 is \(1, 1, 1\), so column operations give zeros quickly.
Plan: \(C_2 - C_1\), \(C_3 - C_1\), then expand and solve.
steps:
Given: \(\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & x & 2 \\ 3 & 6 & x \end{vmatrix} = 0\)
To find: the values of \(x\).
Method: Property vii to make zeros in row 1, then the factorised form gives the roots directly.

Make zeros in row 1
\[C_2 - C_1 \to C_2,\quad C_3 - C_1 \to C_3\]
\[\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & x-2 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 & x-3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\]
Why: Row 2: \(x - 2,\ 2 - 2 = 0\); row 3: \(6 - 3 = 3,\ x - 3\). The value is unchanged.

Triangular determinant
\[1 \cdot (x-2)(x-3) = 0\]
Why: All entries above the diagonal are zero, so the value is the product of the diagonal (Property viii).

Solve
\[x - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2\]
\[x - 3 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 3\]
Why: A product is zero only if a factor is zero.

Check
\[x = 2:\ R_2 = (2, 2, 2) = 2R_1 \Rightarrow \Delta = 0\]
\[x = 3:\ C_1 = (1, 2, 3) = C_3 \Rightarrow \Delta = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Proportional rows or identical columns give a zero determinant.
